q: Which is a sustainable material choice for green buildings?
n: Bamboo is a rapidly renewable resource, making it a sustainable option in eco-friendly construction. Bamboo grows quickly, renews itself and stores carbon, so it is a sustainable material. PVC, imported granite and some laminates have high embodied impacts. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Materials; ISO 22156 (Bamboo Structures).

q: Which of the following refers to custom-fabricated wood components like moldings, trims, stair parts, and paneling installed in interior spaces?
n: Millwork includes architectural wood elements such as crown molding, baseboards, and wall panels that are typically fabricated off-site and customized for interior finishing. Millwork is custom-fabricated wood such as moldings, trims, stair parts and paneling, produced in a mill and installed on site. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: In a kitchen renovation project, which term best describes pre-fabricated modular storage units like base and wall cabinets?
n: Casework refers to factory-made cabinetry, including shelves and cabinets, often used in kitchens, offices, and laboratories for efficient, modular storage solutions. Casework is prefabricated modular cabinetry: base cabinets, wall cabinets and storage units. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI, Casework); CSI MasterFormat Division 12.

q: Which certification should you check when selecting carpets for improved indoor air quality in residential or commercial interiors?
n: CRI Green Label certifies that carpets, adhesives, and cushions emit low levels of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), making them a practical choice for healthier indoor environments. The Carpet and Rug Institute's Green Label (Plus) certifies carpets and adhesives with low VOC emissions for better indoor air quality. Source: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI) Green Label Plus program; LEED v4 EQ Low-Emitting Materials.

q: What is the deadload for a piece of plywood?
n: Per the exam key, the dead load assigned to plywood here is 45 psf. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-1 (Minimum Design Dead Loads) and ASCE 7 commentary tables.

q: What is the ideal use of beadboard in interior applications?
n: Beadboard is typically used for decorative wall treatments such as wainscoting, adding texture and a classic look to interior walls, especially in kitchens, bathrooms, and cottage-style spaces. Beadboard, narrow boards with a bead along each joint, is mainly used as decorative wainscoting on lower walls and as ceiling cladding. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is the recommended open space for this type of lot?
n: Remember that this lot as an interior lot. You can refer to the recommended open space allocation as per Figure 8.2 of the NBCP. For an interior lot, the NBC's recommended open space allocation is about 20–50% of the lot. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Figure VIII.2 (Recommended Open Space Allocation).

q: Which of the following is most suitable for controlling soil erosion on slopes in a site development project?
n: Vetiver plant has deep, dense roots that bind soil effectively, making it ideal for bioengineering solutions in slope stabilization and erosion control during site development. Vetiver grass has deep, dense roots that bind the soil. It is a proven bioengineering method for stabilizing slopes against erosion. Source: World Bank, Vetiver Grass: The Hedge Against Erosion; DPWH slope protection guidelines.

q: Which method is commonly used in site development to achieve instant ground cover and minimize soil erosion on exposed slopes?
n: Sodding involves laying pre-grown grass with soil attached, providing immediate stabilization and erosion control, especially on finished slopes or areas needing quick vegetation cover in site development. Sodding lays pre-grown turf, which covers the ground instantly and protects slopes from erosion at once. Seeding and hydroseeding need time to establish. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Erosion Control); US EPA, Erosion and Sediment Control.

q: Which concept in urban design is Ian Bentley best known for contributing to?
n: Ian Bentley is widely recognized for his work on Responsive Environments, a design framework that promotes urban spaces which support user choice, accessibility, and adaptability, enhancing the livability and legibility of built environments. Ian Bentley is the lead author of Responsive Environments: A Manual for Designers (1985). It sets out principles such as permeability, variety, legibility and robustness. Source: Bentley et al., Responsive Environments (1985).

q: According to Ian Bentley’s urban design principles, which concept refers to the ability of a space to accommodate a variety of uses over time?
n: Robustness, as described by Ian Bentley, is the capacity of a space to support different functions and adapt to changing needs, making it more flexible and sustainable in the long term. In Responsive Environments, robustness is a place's ability to accommodate different uses over time. Source: Bentley et al., Responsive Environments (1985).

q: Combination of paved unroofed open spaces and the building footprint.
n: The construction area is the building footprint plus the paved, unroofed (impervious) areas, that is PSO + ISA. Its maximum is MACA. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.1 (note c).

q: Minimum clear width of Group A dwelling stairs.
n: Stairs in Group A dwellings must have a clear width of at least 750 mm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 708 (Minimum Requirements for Group A Dwellings – Stairs).

q: Minimum depth of foundation.
n: The minimum foundation depth below grade is commonly 600 mm for light buildings on firm soil. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP) (Foundations); NSCP 2015, Ch. 3.

q: Minimum chaflan width.
n: Per the exam key, the chaflan (corner truncation) at street intersections is 4.00 m wide. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Truncated Corners/Chaflan).

q: What is the recommended air movement range for comfortable cooling in interior spaces?
n: Air movement of about 4.6–7.6 m/min (15–25 fpm) is the comfortable range for still-air comfort without draughts. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals, Ch. 9 (Thermal Comfort – Air Speed).

q: What is the required minimum width of door exit according to PD 1096?
n: Per the exam key, the minimum door width given under PD 1096 is 700 mm. Note: exit doors under the Fire Code need at least 810 mm (32 in) clear. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule XII; RA 9514 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5.

q: What is the required minimum width of exit corridor according to the RA 9514?
n: Per the exam key, an exit corridor may be as narrow as 915 mm where the occupant load is under 50. Wider corridors (1,120 mm) are required otherwise. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Exit Access Corridors).

q: Maximum rise height according to the RA 9514.
n: The Fire Code limits riser height to 180 mm, with a minimum tread of 280 mm. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Stairs).

q: What is required if a staircase exceeds 2.24 m in width?
n: Stairs wider than about 2.24 m need intermediate handrails, so every part of the width is within reach of a rail. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 7.2.2.4.1.2; RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR.

q: What is the minimum vehicular impact load for a functional bollard?
n: Per the exam key, a functional (non-crash-rated) bollard should resist a vehicular impact load of about 5,000 lb. Source: ASCE 7, Sec. 4.5.3 (Vehicle Barrier Systems – 6,000 lb) and IBC 1607.9; manufacturers' data.

q: For a commercial building, what is the maximum distance of the off-site parking provisions?
n: Off-site parking for a commercial building must be within 200 m of the building it serves. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking – off-site provisions).

q: For a traffic generating building, what is the minimum distance of its vehicular ingress from a road intersection?
n: Per the exam key, vehicular entrances of traffic-generating buildings should be set back about 50 m from road intersections. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Parking and Access – Traffic Generating Buildings).

q: An esplanade is recommended for waterbodies with easement width of
n: Per the exam key, an esplanade (public walkway) is recommended along waterbodies where the easement is about 9 m or wider. Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51 and NBCP Rule VIII (Easements).

q: What is the recommended distance of the outermost front face of the capitol building to the outer edge of the sidewalk?
n: This refers to the front setback and since the serving road is 12m, the front setback for an institutional building is 5m. The front of the capitol building should be at least 5 m behind the sidewalk, the front setback for an institutional building on that road width. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.3 (Setbacks).

q: In building height computation, EGL means what?
n: EGL means Established Grade Line, the reference elevation from which building height is measured. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Building Height Limit).

q: Which government agency in the Philippines is responsible for mapping, surveying, and providing geospatial data?
n: NAMRIA (National Mapping and Resource Information Authority) is the agency tasked with producing topographic maps, nautical charts, and other geospatial information crucial for land use planning, development, and disaster risk management. NAMRIA (National Mapping and Resource Information Authority) is the national agency for mapping, surveying and geospatial data. Source: Executive Order No. 192 (1987), creation of NAMRIA under the DENR.

q: Which of the following is used to classify the severity of flood hazards in mapping and planning?
n: Flood return period is a statistical measure indicating how often a specific flood level is likely to occur. It is used to classify flood severity, such as 5-year, 10-year, or 100-year floods, helping planners assess risk levels. Per the exam key, flood hazards are classified by return period (such as 5-, 25- and 100-year floods), which indicates how likely a flood level is. Depth is also mapped. Source: NOAH / PAGASA flood hazard mapping; MGB flood susceptibility guidelines.

q: Who reviews and approves CHSP?
n: The Construction Safety and Health Program (CSHP) is submitted to and approved by DOLE before construction begins. Source: DOLE DO 13 s.1998 and DO 198-18 (IRR of RA 11058).

q: Which of the following best describes a typical application of common borrow material in site development?
o: Sub-base for rigid pavement requiring high compaction
General fill for grading and embankment shaping
n: Common borrow is used as a general-purpose fill in areas where specialized properties like high compaction, filtration, or structural load-bearing are not required, making it ideal for grading and shaping embankments. Common borrow is ordinary fill used for general grading and embankments. Select borrow and granular materials are kept for sub-base, filters and structural backfill. Source: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 104 (Embankment) and Item 200 (Aggregate Sub-base).

q: In a typical land use coding, what is the color of industrial zones?
n: Industrial zones are shown in violet (purple) in land-use maps. Residential is yellow and commercial is red. Source: HLURB Guidebook for CLUP Formulation (Land Use Color Codes).

q: What is the Pantone Color of the Year for 2025?
n: Pantone selected Mocha Mousse (PANTONE 17-1230) as the Color of the Year for 2025. This warm, chocolatey brown hue embodies themes of comfort and indulgence, reflecting a global desire for harmony and connection with nature. Its versatility makes it suitable for various applications in fashion, interior design, and branding. Pantone named PANTONE 17-1230 Mocha Mousse its Color of the Year for 2025. Peach Fuzz was 2024's, Ultimate Gray was 2021's (with Illuminating), and Radiant Orchid was 2014's. Source: Pantone Color Institute, Color of the Year 2025 announcement.

q: Which principle best explains why accent walls are commonly painted in darker hues in small residential bedrooms?
n: The principle of advancing and receding colors shows that dark colors can make a wall appear to recede or define depth, creating spatial interest even in compact bedrooms. Darker accent walls appear to recede and add depth. That is the principle of advancing and receding colors. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color – Advancing and Receding); Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: Which of the following is the best wall color for workshop spaces?
n: Per the exam key, light gray is the best wall color for workshops because it is neutral, reflects light well, hides dirt and limits glare. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response (Industrial Color); IES Lighting Handbook (reflectances).

q: What is the main purpose of Le Corbusier’s Modulor system in architecture?
o: To design spaces using human body proportions
To make modular furniture based on ergonometric factors
To guide window sizing using fixed ratios
n: Le Corbusier’s Modulor system uses the human body as a basis for measuring and designing architectural elements, creating spaces that feel natural, functional, and visually harmonious. Le Corbusier's Modulor is a proportioning system based on human body measurements and the golden ratio. It sizes spaces and elements to human scale. Source: Le Corbusier, The Modulor (1948); Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Proportioning Systems).

q: What is the primary reason for regulating Lighting Power Density (LPD) in the Philippine Green Building Code?
n: The Philippine Green Building Code sets LPD (Lighting Power Density) limits to promote energy efficiency by reducing unnecessary power consumption for lighting, contributing to more sustainable and cost-effective building operations. Lighting power density (W/sqm) limits in the Green Building Code cap installed lighting load to promote energy efficiency. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Energy Efficiency – Lighting Power Density.

q: Which of the following is not among the commercially available tinting colors?
n: Universal tinting colors include Burnt Sienna, Phthalo (Thalo) Blue, Lamp Black, Raw Umber and Thalo Green. "Thalo Brown" is not a standard tinting color. Source: Universal tinting color charts (paint manufacturers); ASTM D16.

q: Which of the following spaces is an entrance structure?
n: A porch is a roofed entrance structure attached to a house, sheltering the front door. Terraces, lanais and patios are outdoor living spaces. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.
